news.title: ‘You cannot compare it to our era’: Cafu on Brazil’s decline, 28-year World Cup drought and India clash
news.lede: Navi Mumbai: His words were in Portuguese. His expression, however, reflected love and happiness, just like how he played the game.Standing on stage, as he addressed the enchanted students of Pillai University here, Cafu soaked in the adulation. The smile on his face was constant and matched the one of him in the background poster with that enduring image — of him holding aloft the 2002 FIFA World Cup trophy.More than 24 years later, the hair on his head may have thinned.

news.title: Hull, Asian Cup and the dark arts: Herrington lifts lid on ‘crazy’ rise
news.lede: Since moving to Hull, Lucas Herrington has become the biggest name in Australian football. As the only Aussie in the Premier League he was always destined for that title. Throw in the fact he’s 18, and the excitement around his future is palpable. Lucas Herrington speaks to media.

news.title: FA to canvass England players in World Cup review
news.lede: England's men have not won a major tournament since the 1996 World Cup. The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament. English football's governing body has started the post-tournament review they conduct after every major international competition. The FA says the review is the standard process it undertakes after all tournaments.

news.title: Why are FIFA, UEFA taking legal action in Colorado?
news.lede: DENVER (KDVR) — The 2026 FIFA Men's World Cup ended nearly two months ago, yet the football/soccer world's governing body is back in American headlines, more specifically in Colorado — but why? The litigation follows a lengthy saga including FIFA President Gianni Infantino, the Kushner family, several football confederations worldwide and a recently founded investment firm based here in Denver. Infantino on July 28 announced a plan to create a company to run the World Cup, featuring investments of $4.2 billion from the Kushner family, with other involved parties including Greg Maffei, the CEO and founder of BANN Ventures, which is where the Colorado tie-in comes from. BANN Ventures, founded in 2025, is based in Denver, and its website describes it as an investment firm "dedicated to identifying, backing and scaling companies across the sports, media and entertainment industries."

news.title: The best do not always win the World Cup: Cafu | Football News
news.lede: On a stage at a college atrium, Cafu soaked in the adulation. Students, brandishing any Brazilian jersey they could find – from the present selection with ‘Neymar Jr’ printed on the back to quite a few with ‘Ronaldo’ – cheered him on. Cafu beckoned a few to toss their shirts forward for him to sign and send back.And then his eye caught a replica World Cup trophy. More silver than gold, it was handed over to him to pose with.
